title: The frontend lets a notification be deleted from the dashboard — a submitted one as readily as a draft — and DR1 defines no delete anywhere.

finding.frontend: Every row on the frontend dashboard carries a Delete link (src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/dashboard/view-model/row/actions.js:18-68). It opens a page of its own headed "Delete this notification?" whose only body text is "This cannot be undone.", offering a red "Yes, delete notification" button and a "No, return to dashboard" button (src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/delete-notification/copy/copy.en.js:1-6). The action is not limited to drafts: src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/delete-notification/controller.js:19-22 admits draft, submitted and amending notifications alike, so a notification the authority has already received can be removed from the user's dashboard with one confirmation and no explanation of what that means. Underneath, the record is soft-deleted rather than destroyed, which the page's "This cannot be undone." does not tell the user.
finding.prototype: DR1's dashboard row offers two actions and neither is delete: "Copy as new" and "View" (app/views/dashboard.html:258-262). No DR1 root view, route or link mentions deleting a notification, and the only delete-notification page in the prototype checkout sits under the design-release-2 and design-release-2.1 subtrees, which are later releases and not on trial here. DR1 is not squeamish about deletion in general: its address book gives a saved address a red Delete button on its own view page (app/views/address-book-view.html:43-46). It simply never applies the idea to a notification.
finding.difference: This is a capability the implementation has and the signed-off design does not describe, so there is nothing to bring the frontend into line with and nothing here for a developer to pick up yet. It needs a designer's ruling, and the ruling has to answer three things rather than one: whether a user may delete a notification at all; if so, whether that includes one already submitted to the authority or drafts only; and what the confirmation should say, because "This cannot be undone." is both the whole of the current explanation and not quite true of a soft delete. Until that is answered the finding cannot be settled either way. Nothing in the evidence can settle it — DR1's silence is equally consistent with delete being out of scope and with it having been overlooked.
finding.falsifiedBy: Finding a delete action, a delete confirmation, or any mention of removing a notification in a DR1 root view or route (app/views/*.html, not the design-release-2 or design-release-2.1 subtrees).

relatedTo.why: the same designer's ruling covers both — what a user may do to a notification the authority has already received
